AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

Amazon Web Services (AWS) is looking for an individual to join our Data Center Engineering Operations Team. This committed group works to maintain the critical physical infrastructure that supports Amazon Web Services. Specifically, this team works to ensure that the data center's MEP operates at 100% availability while maintaining first-class customer service to the teams and groups within the data centers.

The Data Center Chief Engineer (CE) is responsible for ensuring that all electrical, mechanical, and fire/life safety equipment within the data center is operating at peak efficiency. This involves planned preventative maintenance of equipment, daily corrective work, and emergency response. The CE serves as an expert technical resource interacting with onsite Engineering Operations Technicians (EOT) and any third party vendors. They are expected to be a singular focal point for all facility operations within a given data center and to support AWS.

Oversee operation and management of routine and emergency services on a variety of critical systems such as: switchgear, generators, UPS systems, power distribution equipment, chillers, cooling towers, computer room air handlers, building monitoring systems, etc
Data Center capacity planning and reporting
May assist in the design and build out of new facilities
Work with IT managers and other business leaders to coordinate projects, manage capacity, and optimize plant safety, performance, reliability and efficiency
Deliver quality service and ensure all customer demands are met
Responsible for asset and inventory management
Respond to out of hours emergency calls – second level escalation point for Data Center acilities related issues / failures

Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related field

Experience in data center engineering or operations

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. About The Role

Anthropic seeks a Head of Enterprise Risk to lead the programs that keep our people, operations, and mission resilient as we scale globally. Reporting to the Head of Resilience Operations, you will own a portfolio of enterprise-risk disciplines — environmental health & safety, access and life-cycle management, third-party (vendor) risk, and the security program management of new facilities — and directly oversee the specialist leaders who run them.

This is a globally strategic role. You set the policy, standards, and frameworks for how enterprise risk is identified, measured, and reduced across the company, and you build the programs — and the team behind them — ahead of need. It’s a fit for a leader who thinks in systems and time horizons and turns forward-looking risk into durable operational programs.

Responsibilities

Enterprise risk management: Own Anthropic’s enterprise risk framework — identify, assess, and prioritize enterprise risks, and integrate risk governance into business planning and decision-making.
Team leadership: Lead and develop a team of programmatic leaders across EH&S, access management, third-party risk, and new-facility security program management; set direction, standards, and accountable outcomes.
EH&S: Enable the global EH&S program leadership and support strategy, policy, and standards development, ensuring regulatory compliance and a strong safety culture across all operations.
Access management: Support the access and life-cycle management leader and their respective programs — access governance, provisioning standards, and auditing — across Anthropic facilities.
Third-party risk: Stand up and run a third-party (vendor) risk program — due diligence, security and safety requirements in contracts, and ongoing monitoring of critical suppliers.
New-facility programs: Facilitate development of the security program management of new facilities — from risk assessment and design requirements through pre-opening readiness and transition to operations — in partnership with regional teams, GSIS, Real Estate, and Facilities.
Horizon scanning: Within the realm of Safety & Security, anticipate emerging enterprise risks tied to rapid growth, new global offices, and frontier research environments, and advise leadership on readiness.
Cross-functional partnership: Partner across GSIS, IT, People, Legal, and Compliance to embed risk programs into the business.

You may be a good fit if you

Have 12+ years in enterprise risk, safety, resilience, or security program leadership, including managing teams and multi-disciplinary programs.
Have built or owned an enterprise risk management framework and integrated it into business planning.
Have led multi-disciplinary programs (e.g., EH&S, access, third-party risk, or facility programs) at organizational scale.
Are an effective people leader who develops specialists and holds a high program bar.
Communicate risk clearly to executives and translate it into operational programs.
Think in systems and time horizons and build ahead of need.
Thrive in fast-paced, high-ambiguity environments.

Strong candidates may have

Considered a leader in your field, with experience building risk, safety, or resilience programs at hyperscale technology companies or across large multi-site, multinational organizations.
A strong EH&S background — program development and oversight in complex or high-risk environments.
Third-party / vendor risk management program experience.
Deep familiarity with enterprise risk frameworks (e.g., ISO 31000) and risk governance.
Relevant certifications (e.g., CSP, CIH, CPP, ARM, or ERM credentials).
Experience in high-profile, regulated, or research environments.

Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us.
To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Description

POSITION SUMMARY:

The Director of Platform Architecture owns the technical design of the shared platform that Briefly's member firms — Rimon, Scale, Caravel and OGC — are consolidating onto. Day to day, the role defines the target-state architecture across identity, integration, security and shared services; sets the standards every application must meet before it goes live at a firm; and leads the technical side of each firm migration.
The position sits within the Transformation Management Office, reports to the VP of Transformation, and works most closely with the Director of Platform Data Operations, the Director of Finance Integration, and IT leadership at each firm. The ideal candidate has built shared infrastructure serving multiple brands or operating companies, is equally comfortable in an architecture review and in a room of partners and can hold a technical standard without alienating the firms who have to live with it.

Essential Functions & Responsibilities

Design the multi-tenant Azure architecture — subscription model, management group hierarchy, tenant isolation boundaries, shared services layer and network topology — sized to serve the current firms and to onboard additional firms without rearchitecting.
Define the Entra ID identity architecture, including tenant topology (single tenant, multi-tenant federation or B2B), single sign-on across all firms and applications, cross-tenant access policies, conditional access, MFA enforcement, and the separation between platform-level and firm-level identity administration.
Design the data partitioning model — row-level security, database isolation, API-layer access controls and audit logging — so that attorney-client privilege boundaries are enforced at every layer of the stack.
Design the matter-level data access control model, translating privilege boundaries into access control lists, data labels, API scopes and audit trails across Aderant, Clio, iManage and the Azure data layer.
Specify the Azure Virtual Desktop architecture for BYOD firms, including pooled versus dedicated session host design, image management, application delivery, and the network path from personal device to managed workspace.
Define the shared services layer — the administrative access pattern that allows a cross-firm support organization to operate across all firms without creating any pathway to cross-firm client data.
Architect the outside counsel guideline compliance posture so that endpoint management, data governance and access logging satisfy the requirements of the firm’s largest corporate clients.
Design the data residency and sovereignty model, covering where data is stored, how it is replicated, and what controls prevent unauthorized cross-border or cross-firm data movement.
Define the audit and monitoring architecture — the logging, alerting and reporting framework that gives firm leadership and the compliance function visibility into who accessed what, when and from where.
Architect the privileged identity management model, granting platform administrators, firm IT administrators and support staff minimum necessary access with just-in-time elevation for sensitive operations.
Define the application registration model governing how Aderant, Clio, iManage, Paylocity, HubSpot and other platform applications integrate with the single sign-on environment across firm boundaries, and the device compliance framework enforced through conditional access.
Produce the migration sequencing plan — which firm migrates in which order, the technical dependencies between migrations, and the parallel-run architecture for each transition.
Design the data migration architecture, covering extraction, transformation and loading patterns for matter data, client records, billing history, trust accounting and document libraries from four separate source systems.
Define the cutover architecture for each firm, including rollback trigger conditions, the hybrid connectivity model that lets users work across legacy and new environments during transition, and the controls that prevent data loss or corruption.
Design the validation framework — the technical tests that must pass before a firm migration is declared complete and legacy systems are decommissioned.
Produce architecture decision records for every significant design choice, documenting the alternatives considered and the rationale for the decision.
Establish architecture governance standards, including the review and approval process for decisions affecting multi-tenancy or data partitioning, and maintain the architecture documentation library and firm-onboarding template.
Serve as the technical reviewer within intake and prioritization, conduct architecture review on vendor selections and major builds, and present architecture decisions, migration progress and platform risk posture to executive leadership on a regular cadence.

Bachelor's degree in computer science, information systems, engineering or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.
Minimum ten years of enterprise architecture experience, including at least three years designing Azure-native multi-tenant solutions.
Demonstrated experience supporting multiple brands, entities or operating companies from a single shared platform.
Deep hands-on expertise with Microsoft Azure, including Entra ID, Azure AD B2C, Azure Virtual Desktop, App Service, API Management, Azure SQL with row-level security, and Azure Monitor.
Demonstrated experience designing single sign-on architectures across multiple organizations using Entra ID, including federated identity, conditional access and cross-tenant access policies.
Proven experience designing data partitioning in multi-tenant environments where tenant isolation is a compliance or regulatory requirement rather than a preference.
Experience architecting migrations from on-premises or heterogeneous cloud environments onto a unified Azure platform, including parallel-run design and staged cutover planning.
Preferred: legal industry experience with attorney-client privilege, matter-level access controls and outside counsel guideline compliance; legal technology platforms such as Aderant, Clio and iManage, including their data models and Azure connectivity; Azure Virtual Desktop as a BYOD access control mechanism; cross-tenant administrative access patterns satisfying zero-trust principles; Microsoft Certified Azure Solutions Architect Expert or equivalent; private-equity-backed or multi-entity professional services environments.

Ability to translate complex technical decisions into business terms for firm leadership and legal professionals.

About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About The Role

Anthropic seeks a Head of Enterprise Risk to lead the programs that keep our people, operations, and mission resilient as we scale globally. Reporting to the Head of Resilience Operations, you will own a portfolio of enterprise-risk disciplines — environmental health & safety, access and life-cycle management, third-party (vendor) risk, and the security program management of new facilities — and directly oversee the specialist leaders who run them.

This is a globally strategic role. You set the policy, standards, and frameworks for how enterprise risk is identified, measured, and reduced across the company, and you build the programs — and the team behind them — ahead of need. It’s a fit for a leader who thinks in systems and time horizons and turns forward-looking risk into durable operational programs.

Responsibilities

Enterprise risk management: Own Anthropic’s enterprise risk framework — identify, assess, and prioritize enterprise risks, and integrate risk governance into business planning and decision-making.
Team leadership: Lead and develop a team of programmatic leaders across EH&S, access management, third-party risk, and new-facility security program management; set direction, standards, and accountable outcomes.
EH&S: Enable the global EH&S program leadership and support strategy, policy, and standards development, ensuring regulatory compliance and a strong safety culture across all operations.
Access management: Support the access and life-cycle management leader and their respective programs — access governance, provisioning standards, and auditing — across Anthropic facilities.
Third-party risk: Stand up and run a third-party (vendor) risk program — due diligence, security and safety requirements in contracts, and ongoing monitoring of critical suppliers.
New-facility programs: Facilitate development of the security program management of new facilities — from risk assessment and design requirements through pre-opening readiness and transition to operations — in partnership with regional teams, GSIS, Real Estate, and Facilities.
Horizon scanning: Within the realm of Safety & Security, anticipate emerging enterprise risks tied to rapid growth, new global offices, and frontier research environments, and advise leadership on readiness.
Cross-functional partnership: Partner across GSIS, IT, People, Legal, and Compliance to embed risk programs into the business.

You may be a good fit if you

Have 12+ years in enterprise risk, safety, resilience, or security program leadership, including managing teams and multi-disciplinary programs.
Have built or owned an enterprise risk management framework and integrated it into business planning.
Have led multi-disciplinary programs (e.g., EH&S, access, third-party risk, or facility programs) at organizational scale.
Are an effective people leader who develops specialists and holds a high program bar.
Communicate risk clearly to executives and translate it into operational programs.
Think in systems and time horizons and build ahead of need.
Thrive in fast-paced, high-ambiguity environments.

Considered a leader in your field, with experience building risk, safety, or resilience programs at hyperscale technology companies or across large multi-site, multinational organizations.
A strong EH&S background — program development and oversight in complex or high-risk environments.
Third-party / vendor risk management program experience.
Deep familiarity with enterprise risk frameworks (e.g., ISO 31000) and risk governance.

Experience in high-profile, regulated, or research environments.

We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. Your safety matters to us.

In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Description

POSITION SUMMARY:

The Director of Platform Architecture owns the technical design of the shared platform that Briefly's member firms — Rimon, Scale, Caravel and OGC — are consolidating onto. Day to day, the role defines the target-state architecture across identity, integration, security and shared services; sets the standards every application must meet before it goes live at a firm; and leads the technical side of each firm migration.
The position sits within the Transformation Management Office, reports to the VP of Transformation, and works most closely with the Director of Platform Data Operations, the Director of Finance Integration, and IT leadership at each firm. The ideal candidate has built shared infrastructure serving multiple brands or operating companies, is equally comfortable in an architecture review and in a room of partners and can hold a technical standard without alienating the firms who have to live with it.

Essential Functions & Responsibilities

Design the multi-tenant Azure architecture — subscription model, management group hierarchy, tenant isolation boundaries, shared services layer and network topology — sized to serve the current firms and to onboard additional firms without rearchitecting.
Define the Entra ID identity architecture, including tenant topology (single tenant, multi-tenant federation or B2B), single sign-on across all firms and applications, cross-tenant access policies, conditional access, MFA enforcement, and the separation between platform-level and firm-level identity administration.
Design the data partitioning model — row-level security, database isolation, API-layer access controls and audit logging — so that attorney-client privilege boundaries are enforced at every layer of the stack.
Design the matter-level data access control model, translating privilege boundaries into access control lists, data labels, API scopes and audit trails across Aderant, Clio, iManage and the Azure data layer.
Specify the Azure Virtual Desktop architecture for BYOD firms, including pooled versus dedicated session host design, image management, application delivery, and the network path from personal device to managed workspace.
Define the shared services layer — the administrative access pattern that allows a cross-firm support organization to operate across all firms without creating any pathway to cross-firm client data.
Architect the outside counsel guideline compliance posture so that endpoint management, data governance and access logging satisfy the requirements of the firm’s largest corporate clients.
Design the data residency and sovereignty model, covering where data is stored, how it is replicated, and what controls prevent unauthorized cross-border or cross-firm data movement.
Define the audit and monitoring architecture — the logging, alerting and reporting framework that gives firm leadership and the compliance function visibility into who accessed what, when and from where.
Architect the privileged identity management model, granting platform administrators, firm IT administrators and support staff minimum necessary access with just-in-time elevation for sensitive operations.
Define the application registration model governing how Aderant, Clio, iManage, Paylocity, HubSpot and other platform applications integrate with the single sign-on environment across firm boundaries, and the device compliance framework enforced through conditional access.
Produce the migration sequencing plan — which firm migrates in which order, the technical dependencies between migrations, and the parallel-run architecture for each transition.
Design the data migration architecture, covering extraction, transformation and loading patterns for matter data, client records, billing history, trust accounting and document libraries from four separate source systems.
Define the cutover architecture for each firm, including rollback trigger conditions, the hybrid connectivity model that lets users work across legacy and new environments during transition, and the controls that prevent data loss or corruption.
Design the validation framework — the technical tests that must pass before a firm migration is declared complete and legacy systems are decommissioned.
Produce architecture decision records for every significant design choice, documenting the alternatives considered and the rationale for the decision.
Establish architecture governance standards, including the review and approval process for decisions affecting multi-tenancy or data partitioning, and maintain the architecture documentation library and firm-onboarding template.
Serve as the technical reviewer within intake and prioritization, conduct architecture review on vendor selections and major builds, and present architecture decisions, migration progress and platform risk posture to executive leadership on a regular cadence.

Minimum Education & Experience Requirements

Bachelor's degree in computer science, information systems, engineering or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.
Minimum ten years of enterprise architecture experience, including at least three years designing Azure-native multi-tenant solutions.
Demonstrated experience supporting multiple brands, entities or operating companies from a single shared platform.
Deep hands-on expertise with Microsoft Azure, including Entra ID, Azure AD B2C, Azure Virtual Desktop, App Service, API Management, Azure SQL with row-level security, and Azure Monitor.
Demonstrated experience designing single sign-on architectures across multiple organizations using Entra ID, including federated identity, conditional access and cross-tenant access policies.
Proven experience designing data partitioning in multi-tenant environments where tenant isolation is a compliance or regulatory requirement rather than a preference.
Experience architecting migrations from on-premises or heterogeneous cloud environments onto a unified Azure platform, including parallel-run design and staged cutover planning.
Preferred: legal industry experience with attorney-client privilege, matter-level access controls and outside counsel guideline compliance; legal technology platforms such as Aderant, Clio and iManage, including their data models and Azure connectivity; Azure Virtual Desktop as a BYOD access control mechanism; cross-tenant administrative access patterns satisfying zero-trust principles; Microsoft Certified Azure Solutions Architect Expert or equivalent; private-equity-backed or multi-entity professional services environments.

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities Requirements

Ability to produce architecture decision records, reference architecture diagrams and migration sequencing plans that non-technical stakeholders can act on.
Ability to translate complex technical decisions into business terms for firm leadership and legal professionals.
Working knowledge of data architecture concepts, including warehouse and lakehouse patterns, master data and reporting layers.
Design judgment under real constraints rather than reliance on vendor reference architectures.
Ability to hold a technical standard under stakeholder pressure and explain the reasoning constructively.
Sound judgment in balancing platform consistency against legitimate firm-specific requirements.
Ability to influence without direct authority across independent business units with their own leadership and budgets.
Strong organizational skills and the ability to manage concurrent workstreams across multiple firms.

Compensation

The base salary range for this position is $180,000 to $220,000 annually. Placement within the range depends on qualifications and relevant experience. The Senior Manager / Director, Business Technology, Sales & Partners leads the technology strategy, delivery, and operations for the Sales and Partner business domains. As the leader of the Sales Partners and Customer Experience Systems Pod, this individual is responsible for the technology roadmap, platform health, delivery execution, and team leadership across Salesforce CRM, CPQ, Service Cloud, Partner Portal, Customer Experience, and related GTM systems. The role translates approved business priorities into secure, scalable technology solutions that improve seller productivity and accelerate revenue growth.

Key Responsibilities

Business Partnership & Strategy

Serve as the primary Business Technology leader for Sales and Partner organizations.
Partner with Sales, Revenue Operations, and Partner stakeholders to develop technology roadmaps aligned to business priorities.
Provide technology guidance, solution options, effort estimates, and delivery tradeoffs to support business decision making.

Project Delivery & Platform Ownership

Own the delivery roadmap and execution for Sales technology platforms including Salesforce CRM, CPQ, Service Cloud, Partner Portal, and related integrations.
Lead prioritization, release planning, capacity management, and delivery across the Sales Systems portfolio.
Ensure platform scalability, security, performance, and operational excellence while reducing technical debt.

Sales, Partners & CX Systems POD Leadership

Lead a cross-functional team of Product Managers, Business Systems Analysts, Developers, Administrators, and QA resources.
Develop team capability, establish clear ownership, and foster a high-performing, customer-focused culture.

Oversee solution design, release governance, platform lifecycle management, and continuous improvement.
Partner with Enterprise Architecture, Security, Integration, and Infrastructure teams to deliver reliable, scalable solutions.

Champion automation, standardization, and continuous process improvement.

10+ years of experience leading Enterprise Business Applications or Business Technology teams.
